description: M4 block transfer. `fetch`: a Fetcher for the given block set root, holders and locally stored CIDs is fed `steps[].event` in order (`at` = clock ms; block bytes are the real block, or "corrupt" = that block with byte [len>>1] XOR 0xff); it must emit exactly `steps[].actions`. `server`: a Server (DEFAULT config unless `config`) must answer each step exactly; lookup serves only the site-basic blocks under the site-basic root.

fetch.why: a single honest BLE holder serves the whole site, batch by batch from the DAG frontier
a block that fails its hash check blames the peer and the same CIDs are re-requested from the next holder
B serves the first batch, then corrupts: blocks already verified are kept and only the rest come from C
no answer by the batch deadline moves on without blame; a tick before the deadline does nothing
when every holder failed the fetch fails (the caller may WANT again)
a block from a peer we did not ask, or for a CID we did not request, changes nothing
adjacent bulk first, then fewest hops; duplicates and holders announcing more than 1 MiB are dropped
blocks already stored (e.g. shared with another site) are never requested
every block is genuine but the site expands past 4 MiB (dedupe bomb): fail, nobody blamed

server.why: known CIDs come back as BLOCK, unknown as BLOCK_NONE, in request order
a request under a root we do not hold gets BLOCK_NONE even for blocks we have
a node with sharing off answers nothing and blames nobody
per-peer bucket: 8 BLOCK_REQs at once, then one per 500 ms
BLOCK / BLOCK_NONE are handed to the fetcher; public gossip or garbage inside a session is blamed
